svg.text: Software is solved. Now be more ambitious.
Writing code is solved. Ambition, taste, verification are not.
7 · Behavior changes: stop → start → try this
Agents out-code humans on A→B tasks
#1 skill in 2026: spot bad agent output, say "no, not like this", then engineer the cause out (see 4b).
A harness is a safe practice copy of the real thing. The agent
can test its own work against it, thousands of times, with no
Why not just use the real YouTube? Real APIs have quotas, keys and rate limits,
change under you, and can't be reset. A fake is free, instant, and always in the same
known state, so the agent can loop for hours alone.
Things you already know that work the same way
The FPS game is the same idea: a CLI plus screenshots lets the agent 'see' and play
its own game, so it can tell whether a change worked.
Judge what the agent made, reject what's wrong, then fix the
cause so it never comes back.
Why it's #1: agents now write the code, but they still can't tell good from
good-enough. The person who keeps saying no, and turns each no into a permanent

Models still lack taste. You define what good
Before any design work, give the agent two or three screenshots you like and one
paragraph on the feel you want.
A one-prompt demo is the floor. Quality comes from
many rounds of expert correction on one product.
Plan for 300 prompts, not one. Each round fixes one specific thing: "spacing too
Make every result reviewable in two minutes, from
Have each agent task end with a preview link, before/after screenshots and a short diff
Guessing the future is a fool's game; act on what
Plan on a 12-month horizon. Re-test your assumptions every time a new model ships.
Effort + caring: the edge, for now. Go bigger.
